history.recommendation_text: The Board reiterated its previous recommendation that the Administration, in coordination with the third- party administrators, investigate newly identified gender- or age-related mismatches in medical diagnoses on a case-by-case basis, ascertain the root causes for those mismatches and take corrective action, including but not limited to requesting the third-party administrators to strengthen monitoring of compliance with the medical insurance reimbursement process.
history.administration_response: As data issues related to gender and/or age could result in apparent mismatches in medical diagnoses, data disparity reports are being provided by third-party administrators after each eligibility tape is processed to ensure the alignment of the demographic and eligibility status of active and retired health insurance participants. The third-party administrator’s claim adjudication processes and related elements regarding medical necessity mitigates against mismatches in medical diagnoses. In addition, the health insurance claims audits currently being conducted by a third-party external audit firm will also provide assurance as to the appropriate processing of health insurance claims by the third-party administrators. Based on the actions taken, the Administration considers this recommendation implemented and requests that it be considered closed.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Administration has implemented a claim verification process to prevent mismatches in medical diagnoses, the Board considers this recommendation to be implemented.
